Marathon Petroleum has fallen 0.7% today, extending a sharp two-week drop of 8.8% that accelerated over the last week. The slide reflects weakness in oil and refining margins: US crude is trading at $89.53 per barrel, down from levels that would have supported higher refinery profits, and with refineries running at 95.7% capacity and storage inventories elevated (694 million barrels of oil, 216 million barrels of gasoline in storage), there's less urgency for refined products—the main profit driver for refiners like Marathon.

Geopolitical risks to global oil supply—including Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, Iranian tanker incidents near the Hormuz Strait, and attacks on Russian refineries—haven't pushed crude prices higher, suggesting markets are skeptical these will severely disrupt flows. That leaves refiners competing on thinner margins in an oversupplied environment.
